english: how are you doing?; how's it going?
use: A casual greeting between friends or coworkers; answer with bochibochi, aikawarazu da yo or genki da yo.

example.romaji: yaa, saikin choushi dou? isogashii?
example.ja: やあ、最近調子どう？忙しい？
example.english: Hey, how's it going lately? Busy?

examplePolite.romaji: ohisashiburi desu. saikin choushi wa dou desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: お久しぶりです。最近調子はどうですか？
examplePolite.english: It's been a while. How have you been lately?

notes: Also asks about one specific thing: ashi no choushi dou? (how's your leg?).

src: 何か変わったことあった？
ja: 何か変わったことあった？
kana: なにかかわったことあった？
politeJa: 何か変わったことありましたか？
english: anything new with you?
use: Asked when you catch up after time apart; if nothing's new, answer betsu ni or aikawarazu da yo.

example.romaji: hisashiburi da ne. nanika kawatta koto atta?
example.ja: 久しぶりだね。何か変わったことあった？
example.english: It's been a while. Anything new with you?

examplePolite.romaji: saikin, nanika kawatta koto arimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 最近、何か変わったことありましたか？
examplePolite.english: Has anything new happened lately?

notes: Kawatta koto means 'anything different'; kawatta hito means 'an odd person'.

english: are you off today?; is it your day off?
use: Asked when you bump into someone at a time they'd usually be working.

example.romaji: are, kyou wa yasumi? shigoto ja nai no?
example.ja: あれ、今日は休み？仕事じゃないの？
example.english: Oh, are you off today? No work?

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa oyasumi desu ka? ii desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 今日はお休みですか？いいですね。
examplePolite.english: Are you off today? Nice.

notes: About a shop, the same words ask whether it's closed today.

politeJa: ご家族はお元気ですか？
english: how's your family?
use: Asked of a friend you haven't seen for a while; answer un, minna genki da yo (yeah, everyone's well).

example.romaji: sou ieba, kazoku wa genki? okaasan mo?
example.ja: そういえば、家族は元気？お母さんも？
example.english: By the way, how's your family? Your mum too?

examplePolite.romaji: sou ieba, gokazoku wa ogenki desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: そういえば、ご家族はお元気ですか？
examplePolite.english: By the way, how is your family?

notes: The polite form honours their family with go- and o-; never use those for your own family.

kana: すずしくなってきたね
politeJa: 涼しくなってきましたね
english: it's getting cooler, isn't it
use: Seasonal small talk in early autumn with neighbours, coworkers, anyone; just agree with sou da ne.

example.romaji: asaban, daibu suzushiku natte kita ne.
example.ja: 朝晩、だいぶ涼しくなってきたね。
example.english: It's really getting cooler in the mornings and evenings.

examplePolite.romaji: asaban, daibu suzushiku natte kimashita ne.
examplePolite.ja: 朝晩、だいぶ涼しくなってきましたね。
examplePolite.english: It's really getting cooler in the mornings and evenings.

notes: Swap the adjective for other seasons: atsuku natte kita ne (getting hot), samuku natte kita ne (getting cold).

english: same as ever; nothing much new
use: Answer to choushi dou? or saikin dou? when nothing has changed.

example.romaji: un, aikawarazu da yo. shigoto bakkari.
example.ja: うん、相変わらずだよ。仕事ばっかり。
example.english: Yeah, same as ever. All work.

examplePolite.romaji: hai, aikawarazu desu. shigoto bakari de.
examplePolite.ja: はい、相変わらずです。仕事ばかりで。
examplePolite.english: Yes, same as ever. Just work.

notes: Also says someone hasn't changed, often teasing: aikawarazu da ne (you haven't changed a bit).

politeJa: バタバタしていました
english: things have been hectic; I've been rushed off my feet
use: Explains why you've been out of touch or slow to reply, often after gomen.

example.romaji: gomen, kongetsu zutto batabata shiteta.
example.ja: ごめん、今月ずっとバタバタしてた。
example.english: Sorry, it's been hectic all month.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, kongetsu zutto batabata shite imashita.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、今月ずっとバタバタしていました。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, it's been hectic all month.

notes: Batabata is the sound of rushing around; for right now say ima batabata shiteru (I'm swamped).

english: so-so; getting by; not bad
use: Modest answer to how's it going or how's business; strongly Kansai but understood everywhere.

example.romaji: shigoto? maa, bochibochi da ne.
example.ja: 仕事？まあ、ぼちぼちだね。
example.english: Work? Oh, getting by.

examplePolite.romaji: shigoto desu ka? maa, bochibochi desu.
examplePolite.ja: 仕事ですか？まあ、ぼちぼちです。
examplePolite.english: Work? Oh, getting by.

notes: Also means 'about time, little by little': bochibochi kaerou ka (shall we head home soon?).

english: I haven't been sleeping enough; a bit short on sleep
use: Said when someone asks if you're okay or says you look tired.

example.romaji: un, daijoubu. chotto nebusoku nan da.
example.ja: うん、大丈夫。ちょっと寝不足なんだ。
example.english: Yeah, I'm fine. Just a bit short on sleep.

examplePolite.romaji: daijoubu desu. chotto nebusoku nan desu.
examplePolite.ja: 大丈夫です。ちょっと寝不足なんです。
examplePolite.english: I'm fine. Just a bit short on sleep.

notes: Nebusoku is a noun: nebusoku de atama ga itai (my head hurts from lack of sleep).

politeJa: なんとかやっています
english: getting by; hanging in there
use: Answer to how's it going when things are tough but okay; sounds modest and a bit tired.

example.romaji: shigoto wa taihen da kedo, nantoka yatteru yo.
example.ja: 仕事は大変だけど、なんとかやってるよ。
example.english: Work's tough, but I'm getting by.

examplePolite.romaji: shigoto wa taihen desu kedo, nantoka yatte imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 仕事は大変ですけど、なんとかやっています。
examplePolite.english: Work's tough, but I'm getting by.

notes: Nantoka means 'somehow'; nantoka naru (it'll work out somehow) is a common pair.

polite: ii n ja nai desu ka?
politeJa: いいんじゃないですか？
english: sounds good to me; why not?; I think it's fine
use: Approves a friend's plan, outfit or choice; a flat tone can sound like 'whatever'.

example.romaji: sono fuku, ii n ja nai? niau yo.
example.ja: その服、いいんじゃない？似合うよ。
example.english: That outfit's nice, I think. It suits you.

examplePolite.romaji: sono an, ii n ja nai desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: その案、いいんじゃないですか？
examplePolite.english: That idea sounds good to me.

notes: Not a negative: ja nai? here means 'isn't it?'.

english: not bad; pretty good
use: Mild praise that often means 'actually quite good'; tone decides how warm it is.

example.romaji: kono mise, warukunai ne. mata koyou.
example.ja: この店、悪くないね。また来よう。
example.english: This place isn't bad. Let's come again.

examplePolite.romaji: kono mise, warukunai desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: この店、悪くないですね。
examplePolite.english: This place isn't bad.

notes: Also 'it's not your fault': kimi wa warukunai yo.

english: I don't mind it; I kind of like it
use: A shy or understated way to say you like something; it usually means more than it says.

example.romaji: kou iu ongaku, kirai ja nai yo.
example.ja: こういう音楽、嫌いじゃないよ。
example.english: I kind of like this kind of music.

examplePolite.romaji: kou iu ongaku, kirai ja nai desu.
examplePolite.ja: こういう音楽、嫌いじゃないです。
examplePolite.english: I kind of like this kind of music.

notes: Said about a person it can be a coy confession of liking them.

polite: mite son wa nai desu yo
english: it's worth a watch; you won't regret seeing it
use: Recommends a film, show or sight to a friend.

example.romaji: ano eiga, ichido mite son wa nai yo.
example.ja: あの映画、一度見て損はないよ。
example.english: That film's worth seeing at least once.

examplePolite.romaji: ano eiga, ichido mite son wa nai desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: あの映画、一度見て損はないですよ。
examplePolite.english: That film's worth seeing at least once.

notes: Works with other verbs: itte son wa nai (worth going), yonde son wa nai (worth reading).

english: that works; that's an option; I'm into that
use: Says an idea or combination is acceptable or even good; the opposite is nashi (no way).

example.romaji: piza ni painappuru? un, ari da ne.
example.ja: ピザにパイナップル？うん、アリだね。
example.english: Pineapple on pizza? Yeah, that works.

examplePolite.romaji: sono kangae, ari desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: その考え、アリですね。
examplePolite.english: That idea could work.

notes: Ari ka nashi ka? (yes or no?) asks whether something's acceptable.

kana: わたしにはあわなかった
politeJa: 私には合わなかったです
english: it wasn't for me; it didn't suit me
use: A polite way to dislike something without calling it bad; it puts the problem on your taste.

example.romaji: ano manga, watashi ni wa awanakatta na.
example.ja: あの漫画、私には合わなかったな。
example.english: That manga wasn't really for me.

examplePolite.romaji: ano manga wa, watashi ni wa awanakatta desu.
examplePolite.ja: あの漫画は、私には合わなかったです。
examplePolite.english: That manga wasn't for me.

notes: Also for food or medicine that disagrees with you. Present tense: watashi ni wa awanai.

english: not quite there; a bit lacking; so-so
use: Says food, a film or an idea falls a bit short; softer than mazui or tsumaranai.

example.romaji: kono raamen, aji ga imaichi da na.
example.ja: このラーメン、味がいまいちだな。
example.english: This ramen's a bit meh.

examplePolite.romaji: kono raamen, aji ga imaichi desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: このラーメン、味がいまいちですね。
examplePolite.english: The flavour of this ramen is a bit lacking.

notes: Before a verb it means 'not quite': imaichi wakaranai (I don't quite get it).

src: あんまり好きじゃない
ja: あんまり好きじゃない
kana: あんまりすきじゃない
politeJa: あまり好きじゃないです
english: I'm not that keen on it; I don't really like it
use: The everyday soft way to say you dislike something; kirai is much stronger.

example.romaji: horaa eiga wa anmari suki ja nai n da.
example.ja: ホラー映画はあんまり好きじゃないんだ。
example.english: I'm not really into horror films.

examplePolite.romaji: horaa eiga wa amari suki ja nai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: ホラー映画はあまり好きじゃないんです。
examplePolite.english: I'm not really into horror films.

notes: Anmari is the spoken form of amari; it needs a negative after it.

english: something's off; not quite it
use: Said when something isn't what you wanted but you can't say why: a haircut, a recipe, a word.

example.romaji: kono iro, nanka chigau na. betsu no ni shiyou.
example.ja: この色、なんか違うな。別のにしよう。
example.english: This colour's not quite right. Let's go with another.

examplePolite.romaji: kono iro, nanka chigaimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: この色、なんか違いますね。
examplePolite.english: This colour isn't quite right.

notes: Nanka means 'somehow, kind of'; chigau alone means 'that's wrong' or 'that's different'.

src: 期待してたほどじゃなかった
ja: 期待してたほどじゃなかった
kana: きたいしてたほどじゃなかった
polite: kitai shite ita hodo ja nakatta desu
politeJa: 期待していたほどじゃなかったです
english: it wasn't as good as I'd hoped
use: Mild disappointment about a film, restaurant or trip that had been hyped.

example.romaji: hyouban ii kedo, kitai shiteta hodo ja nakatta.
example.ja: 評判いいけど、期待してたほどじゃなかった。
example.english: It's got great reviews, but it wasn't as good as I'd hoped.

examplePolite.romaji: hyouban wa ii desu kedo, kitai shite ita hodo ja nakatta desu.
examplePolite.ja: 評判はいいですけど、期待していたほどじゃなかったです。
examplePolite.english: It's got great reviews, but it wasn't as good as I'd hoped.

notes: Hodo ja nai means 'not as much as'; omotta hodo ja nakatta (not as ... as I thought) is the same idea.
